requirements.requirement: A host firewall is enabled on node1 and persists (enabled at boot) via ufw/systemd
requirements.summary: ufw was enabled with --force enable, systemctl is-enabled ufw returned 'enabled', and ufw status verbose showed 'active' both immediately after configuration (cmd-ba997be5fd7b442f) and after a full reboot (cmd-c0e05ca2e0f14adf), with the boot-identity observation confirming an actual restart occurred (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity -> global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity).

Explicit ufw allow rule for 22/tcp was added and shown active in ufw status, and confirmed at the kernel level via nft ruleset showing 'tcp dport 22 ... accept' in both IPv4 and IPv6 chains, both pre- and post-reboot.

Explicit ufw allow rule for 8080/tcp added and enforced at kernel level (nft accept rule for dport 8080), and directly demonstrated with a live test: a temporary listener on 8080 returned HTTP 200 when reached externally, confirming the port is actually reachable through the firewall.

Default incoming policy set to reject (ufw), implemented at the kernel as an nftables input chain 'policy drop' with no accept rule for other ports; a live test to an unrelated port (9999) was refused ('Connection refused', nc exit 1), directly demonstrating enforcement rather than just configuration.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration survives a node restart (implied by 'persistent' in the task instruction)
requirements.summary: A full node1 reboot was performed with a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id captured, ufw active/enabled), a background reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polling that showed a connection timeout during the reboot window followed by a new boot_id, and a post-restart re-verification showing ufw active/enabled with identical default policy and allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots which independently confirm the boot_id changed from 4d70780a... to ea1bf088....

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task contract: a persistent ufw-based firewall on node1 permits SSH and TCP 8080 while rejecting other inbound traffic, verified at configuration time, at the kernel (nftables) level, via live connection tests (8080 reachable, an unrelated port refused), and confirmed to survive a full node reboot with identical rules and active/enabled state afterward. The mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol was also completed with a clean pre/post boot-identity transition corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Only one unrelated port (9999) was tested for rejection; broader port-scan evidence was not captured, though the nftables ruleset dump independently confirms no other accept rules exist.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured for the restart-persistence check; no additional stress (e.g., repeated reboots or service restarts) was observed.
IPv6 reachability of SSH/8080 was inferred from nftables rule presence but not live-tested (only IPv4 curl/nc tests were run).

operational_hygiene.summary: The only mutation not directly part of the firewall configuration itself was a temporary Python HTTP server bound to port 8080 (cmd-0643c807755f4cb8), started solely to produce live evidence that the allowed port is reachable through the firewall. It was fully cleaned up in the same session (cmd-ae3a1fe6d110492f: process killed, pid/log files removed), and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot confirms no residual listener remains. The single-node reboot (cmd-3af7e312c8024cd6) was a bounded, required action tied to the mandatory restart-evidence protocol, not an unnecessary mutation. No abandoned files, failed services, or unrelated configuration changes are present in the after-executor snapshot relative to after-prepare (aside from the expected boot-identity and socket ordering changes from the reboot itself, plus fresh systemd-private temp directories that are normal post-boot artifacts).
